question: Should OpenClaw add dynamic ack reaction selection, and if so should the permanent contract be a configured emoji array, deterministic/random selector, rule-based strategy, or model-driven pre-ack hook?
rationale: This changes a shipped cross-channel config/API surface, and ack reactions are emitted before normal reply generation, so code inspection cannot choose the user-facing semantics or compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Approve a shared selector contract
options.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction` or `ackReactions` selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

options.title: Keep single-value ack reactions
options.body: Leave variability to lifecycle status reactions or manual `message(action=react)` calls and close or defer this feature direction.

options.title: Design an extension seam first
options.body: Define a plugin/channel hook for pre-ack selection before adding new core config semantics.

recommendation.title: Approve a shared selector contract
recommendation.body: Add a backward-compatible shared `ackReaction` or `ackReactions` selector strategy that preserves existing string configs and is implemented consistently across supported channels.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest shared-helper history and prior review context for this exact ack-reaction surface.
